stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{\left(- x - 1\right) \left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 4\right)} \). Find every vertical asymptote of the graph of f, and state the one sided limits of f at each one.

answer_key.label: Only \( x = -4 \) is a vertical asymptote, with \( \lim_{x \to -4^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to -4^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).

worked_solution.text: Factor and cancel: for \( x \ne -1 \), \( f(x) = \frac{1 - x}{x + 4} \). The factor at \( x = -1 \) divides out, so that break is removable, with no asymptote.
The remaining denominator is 0 only at \( x = -4 \), where the numerator of the reduced expression is 5, not 0.
The denominator \( x + 4 \) is negative just left of -4 and positive just right of it, so \( \lim_{x \to -4^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to -4^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the quotient on each side

options.label: No line is a vertical asymptote, because \( \lim_{x \to -4^{+}} f(x) = \infty \) is a limit that exists at \( x = -4 \).
options.derivation: the infinite one sided limit read as an existing limit, so no asymptote is recognised

options.label: Both \( x = -1 \) and \( x = -4 \) are vertical asymptotes, with \( \lim_{x \to -4^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to -4^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).
options.derivation: a vertical asymptote named at the zero of the denominator whose factor divides out

options.label: Only \( x = -4 \) is a vertical asymptote, with \( \lim_{x \to -4} f(x) = \infty \) from both sides.
options.derivation: one two sided infinite limit written although the two sides have opposite signs
